Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Friday, August 14, 2026, and we're starting the day with a high of 95° and air quality at a moderate 56. Overnight, police and fire crews handled a mix of calls — from a welfare check for a woman seen crying in a red pickup to a high-speed DUI south of the Grapevine. The top story this morning: Kern County supervisors are exploring a proposal to split California into two states, a move aimed at ensuring Kern's voice is heard in Sacramento. Let's get to the news.

## The Kern Overnight

The overnight hours brought a mix of law enforcement activity and a few calls for fire crews. Around 9:23 p.m., city units were dispatched to White Lane for a road-rage disturbance involving a blue Honda with paper plates and a white pickup, both repeatedly stopping and blocking the roadway eastbound. Then, at 10:33 p.m., a white 2001 Dodge van with California plates was reported stolen on Kentucky Street; officers took the report, and no arrests were announced on the air. Later, around 11:34 p.m., police broadcast an urgent attempt-to-locate and welfare check after a caller described an older-model red truck at South Chester Avenue and Belle Terrace — a male was seen hanging out the driver's window, while a female was crying and saying she needed help. The truck was last seen traveling southbound, and the broadcast went out citywide for any unit to catch it. Around 11:39 p.m., CHP broadcast a DUI on southbound I-5 south of the Grapevine involving a newer black pickup at speeds over 90 mph, with the driver seen drinking from an open container. Fire crews were comparatively quiet: a residential alarm on Greenview Lane around 11 p.m. amounted to nothing, and a vehicle accident drew an engine, battalion, and rescue unit before the air went quiet. Early this morning, shortly before 3 a.m., a traffic collision occurred in the Flying J truck stop parking lot at Frazier Park, where a burgundy Freightliner was hit by a red Peterbilt, with the other party denying involvement.

## Today's weather

Today's weather will see a high near 95° and a low around 67° tonight. It's currently 84° at Meadows Field (KBFL). There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and air quality is at a moderate 56.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that Kern County supervisors are exploring a proposal to split California into two states**, a move aimed at ensuring Kern's voice is heard in Sacramento. Kern County District 3 Supervisor Jeff Flores said the effort is about making sure the region's industries and way of life are taken seriously by state leaders. An analysis presented to the board found the proposed inland state would account for only about 15 percent of California's current real GDP. CSU Bakersfield economics professor Richard Gearhart said that number tells a stark story about what separation would actually mean for the region.

**According to 23ABC, Bakersfield police and fire chiefs shared their Fourth of July findings at a recent meeting**, revealing both progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents in the city. Kevin Albertson, Chief of the Bakersfield Fire Department, said the holiday brought serious consequences for people across the state. A total of 106 citations were issued by the Bakersfield Police and Fire departments combined in relation to the holiday. Compared to 2025, fire-related responses to both departments dropped 6% in 2026. Despite the decrease, residents and officials say more work remains.

**23ABC also tells us that Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, helped shape a federal best practices toolkit aimed at addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community**. Baldovinos traveled to San Diego on August 12 to celebrate the public release of the toolkit, a project he helped build from the ground up. He was among roughly 22 professionals from across the country who gathered in Washington, D.C., in the spring to work with the Trump administration, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the Department of Health and Human Services, and the nation's drug czar to develop the toolkit. The toolkit outlines best practices for working with individuals dealing with addiction within the homeless population, covering topics including program length, transitional housing, long-term mentorship, and workforce development.

## Something good

Bakersfield and Tehachapi airports will benefit from a portion of $109 million in federal aviation funding. This investment will support improvements and upgrades at local airports.

## Coming up this week

This week, several public meetings and events are worth noting. On Tuesday, August 18, the Multi Modal Transportation And Traffic Safety Committee meets at 12:00 p.m., followed by the Historic Preservation Commission at 4:00 p.m. and the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission at 2:00 p.m. On Wednesday, August 19, the Water Board meets at 10:00 a.m. On Thursday, August 20, the Planning Commission meets at 5:30 p.m. Today, Friday, August 14, the Special Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee meets at 1:00 p.m., and the Keep Bakersfield Beautiful Committee meets at 12:00 p.m. Also today, the Special Laws and Legislation Committee meets at 12:00 p.m. Looking ahead to next week, several events are on the calendar at the Fox Theater: PEPPER With CYDEWAYS on August 14, Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio on August 22, Rodney Carrington on August 27, CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on August 28, Willie Barcena on August 29, and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix on August 29.
